objective: Give FormField's Field two layouts besides today's stacked one, a checkbox layout (the box before its label on one line) and a row layout (the control and one trailing action side by side under the label), and adopt them: EmailPreference uses the checkbox layout, so Notifications.module.css's .preference > div exception into Field's markup is deleted, and the search bar's box and Search button sit in one row through SearchInput's new action prop.
acceptance_criteria: Start gate: agent/FRONTEND-053 is cut from the tip of the integration branch outstanding-track-5 after the FRONTEND-052 budget fold (bundle-budgets/FRONTEND-052.ts is gone and BASE.lazy has ScrollTable: 283).

Test-first: commit the failing tests alone before the implementation, with frontend/src/test/bundle-budgets/FRONTEND-053.ts. The new tests fail today because Field has no layout prop, SearchInput has no action prop and FormField.module.css has no .checkbox or .row rule.

Field (frontend/src/components/FormField.tsx) takes an optional prop layout?: "stack" | "checkbox" | "row", default "stack". With no layout, or "stack", the markup is exactly today's: a root div with the field class only, then label, the children, the hint, the error. auth/form-field.test.tsx stays untouched and green.

Checkbox layout: the root div carries the field class and a checkbox class from FormField.module.css. DOM order is the children (the checkbox input, a direct child of the root), then the label, then the hint, then the error. The ids, label htmlFor, describeField's aria-describedby and aria-invalid are unchanged, so the box's accessible name and description are unchanged. A new test pins the order, the class, the name and the description.

Checkbox layout CSS, in FormField.module.css only: .checkbox is a wrapping row (flex-direction: row; flex-wrap: wrap), items centred, at least var(--target-min) high; the checkbox input is 1.25rem square, flex: none, margin 0; the label takes the remaining width (flex: 1) so the whole line is the hit area; the hint and the error each take a line of their own (flex-basis: 100%); cursor: pointer is set only through selectors that contain :enabled (the input and the label after an enabled input), and at least one such rule exists. Tests read these from disk.

Row layout: the root div carries the field class and a row class. DOM order is the label, the children in order, the hint, the error. CSS in FormField.module.css: .row is display: grid with grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) auto and a column gap from a space token, and the label, the hint and the error span the full row (grid-column: 1 / -1), so the first child (the control) takes the room and a second child (an action) keeps its own width beside it. Tests read these from disk.

SearchInput (frontend/src/components/ui/SearchInput.tsx) takes an optional action?: ReactNode. Without it, SearchInput renders exactly as today (stack layout; every existing SearchInput.test.tsx test stays green). With it, SearchInput passes layout="row" to Field and renders the action after the icon's wrapper, as the Field root's last child before the hint and error. New tests in SearchInput.test.tsx pin both cases.

SearchBar (frontend/src/features/search/SearchBar.tsx) passes its Search button to SearchInput as action: the box and the button share the box's Field root, the button follows the box, and both stay inside the form role="search". The button keeps type="submit", the name Search, variant primary and size md; the box keeps its label, name="q", the 100 cap and BOX_ID. A new test in SearchBar.test.tsx pins the shared root and the order; every existing SearchBar, SearchPage and search-* test stays untouched and green (the home rail and /search use the one SearchBar).

Search.module.css: the .bar rules that stacked the box over the button (.bar, .bar input) are deleted, and SearchBar's form no longer uses a .bar class. SearchInput's own .wrapper .input already sets the box's width. No other search rule changes.

EmailPreference (frontend/src/features/notifications/EmailPreference.tsx) passes layout="checkbox" to its Field; nothing else in it changes (the label text, EMAIL_FIELD_ID, the hint, the alert, the optimistic mutation). Notifications.module.css keeps .preference (the card's own column of field and alert) and deletes every rule that reaches into Field's markup: .preference > div, .preference input[type="checkbox"], .preference label, the two cursor rules and .preference > div > p, with the comment above them. A new test pins that no selector in Notifications.module.css reaches inside .preference (no .preference followed by a combinator or a descendant), and that the checkbox's Field root has the checkbox class and the box precedes its label.

Two existing tests pin the deleted exception, so the test commit changes them, and only them, in frontend/src/features/notifications/notifications-style.test.tsx under "the unavailable-email caption (NOTIFICATIONS-002)": "wraps to its own line under the row, rather than squeezing the label" reads FormField.module.css's .checkbox rules instead of .preference > div (flex-wrap: wrap on .checkbox; flex-basis: 100% for its hint), and "does not leave cursor: pointer on a disabled control or its label" reads FormField.module.css instead of Notifications.module.css; the FIELD_ROW constant and its comment go with them. Their intent (the caption takes its own line; no pointer on a disabled box) is unchanged. Every other existing test is untouched.

CSS rule checks keep passing: the module-CSS scans (src/test/module-css.ts, src/test/css.ts and their callers, including auth-css.test.ts for FormField.module.css, notifications-css.test.ts, search-css.test.ts and components/ui/ui-css.test.ts), the tokens and base checks under src/styles/. Every value in the new rules is a token or a unitless/rem size as above; no px font size, no colour.

Bundle: the test commit adds frontend/src/test/bundle-budgets/FRONTEND-053.ts declaring entryJsGzipGrowth, entryJsRawGrowth and entryCssGzipGrowth, each the growth measured with this test's build on the finished implementation rounded up to the next 100 B, and changed: { "css:NotificationsPage.css": N }, N its measured gzip rounded up to the next 100 B. The Director's prototype measured entry JS +96 B gzip and +161 B raw, entry CSS +112 B and css:NotificationsPage.css 496 to 368 B, so expect about 100, 200, 200 and 400. entryJsGzipGrowth must stay within ENTRY_GROWTH_PER_UNIT_MAX (1000); if it would not, stop and report. If any other lazy output appears, disappears or moves past the 100 B tolerance, stop and record it. bundle-budget.ts is not touched and no budget is loosened.

Proof: npm run lint reports 0 problems; npm run typecheck and npm run build are green; the suite runs in the foreground, alone, sharded (npx vitest run --shard=N/3 --maxWorkers=2), and the PR records the shard counts and the measured bundle numbers.
No new dependency; no change outside the allowed paths; no change to other Field callers (the auth pages, compose, profile, account, stats): they keep the stack layout by default.

Module docs: wiki/CodeContext/Modules/0x08-frontend.md's src/components row says Field has stack (default), checkbox and row layouts; 0x08a-frontend-shell.md's SearchInput entry names the action prop and the row layout, and that SearchBar's box and button sit in one row; 0x08e-frontend-notifications.md replaces the .preference > div text (the NOTIFICATIONS-002 entry and the UI-007 preference-card entry) with EmailPreference using Field's checkbox layout, the caption on its own line and the pointer only while enabled now being Field's.

Browser check (the Director's, after merge; not the unit's): the notifications preference card (available and unavailable states) and the search bar on /search and in the home rail (from 1217 px wide), in light and dark, at 360 and 1280 px wide: the box sits before its label on one line with the caption under it; the search box and button sit in one row with the button's full label visible and the box still usable in the 288 px rail; focus rings and the 44 px targets are intact.
